Looks like you forgot to check in the result of this generation.
Acknowledged
Please take a look at the existing structures we have for redfish Message registries. What you've implemented here looks like a duplicate.

The reason I'm doing this (making a separate structure) is, because the code using message registries get registry name and message ID, so it can load the registry and look for the message id in there.
The code I'm writing gets dbus event id as an input, and here we have 2 options:
1. Put lists of dbus events that should be mapped to particular message ID into existing message registry structures. In this case we will not need an additional structure, but we will need to traverse ALL the message registries looking for a messageID associated with the received dbus event name.
2. Have a separate structure where each key points to particular registry and message id. You may think of it as an index. Since it's pre-generated and requires traversal only thru this index, it's much faster and cheaper that #1.

> The reason I'm doing this (making a separate structure) is, because the code using message registries get registry name and message ID, so it can load the registry and look for the message id in there.

As a description, that code is identical to what exists.  Aside from pulling this information from dbus instead of journald, the differences in the actual redfish code here is negligeble, and a lot of effort has been spent already to keep the existing structures:
A. No cost to construct at startup
B. No sustained memory usage

> The code I'm writing gets dbus event id as an input, and here we have 2 options:
> 1. Put lists of dbus events that should be mapped to particular message ID into existing message registry structures. In this case we will not need an additional structure, but we will need to traverse ALL the message registries looking for a messageID associated with the received dbus event name.

Keep in mind, the existing lists are sorted, so this is a Log(N) search per registry to search, but given we know the prefix..... don't we know which registry to search for the ID?

> 2. Have a separate structure where each key points to particular registry and message id. You may think of it as an index. Since it's pre-generated and requires traversal only thru this index, it's much faster and cheaper that #1.

Lets start with the naive, simple version (keep changes incremental) and we can write a patch that "shows" (ideally with performance numbers) that we need a new structure.

Stepping back from data structures for a second:

This is the part I'm not understanding.  Redfish needs arguments as indexes (%1, %2, %3, etc) to be able to do message string replacement from the registry template string and args.

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/da9dc905da4e6d30125bcca160537cf2cdb2ddf4/redfish-core/include/registries.hpp#L47C20-L47C35

As we've defined the dbus interface, where is that mapping coming from?  PDI?

I have a minor preference for "Use existing structures." option (because it keeps the structs the same). There's already some args that are per-argument, so combining them into a new struct, like

MessageArg{
   std::string_view dbusArgName;  <- will be empty string for registries not generated from PDI
   std::string_view argType;  <- needs retained in both cases.
}

struct Message
{
...
std::array<const MessageArg, 5> paramTypes;
}

Seems worthwhile.  

Can you elaborate on what the dbusMessageName arg would be or do?  I expected that PDI -> messageId translation would be a mechanical transform (snake case to CamelCase, etc) and not that we'd have to store a separate string.  I'm happy to declare the mapping around "Openbmc LeakDetectedCritical translates to Redfish Environmental LeakDetectedCritical" type map here... but I think Patricks intent was for that to live in PDI (and that's probably a more proper place for it).

Keep in mind, there's a boatload of Redfish MessageIds, and we have 1MB of binary space to play with, so some of the data structure intent here is trying to keep the binary data small, constexpr, in RODATA, and deduplicated as much as possible down to only what redfish needs so that we don't explode the binary when we pull in DMTF  where where we might use 10% of the messages in them.

> As we've defined the dbus interface, where is that mapping coming from? PDI?

Yes, the mapping is coming from PDI. Let me explain how it works.
PDI defines DBus structs. Patrick added optional fields, that contain mapping info. When PDI repo is being built, registry files are generated. They are DMTF RegistryFiles, but in Oem properties they get mapping data populated. Mapping data looks like this:
```
"OpenBMC_Mapping": {
            "xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.ReadingBelowUpperSoftShutdownThreshold": {
                "RedfishEvent": "SensorEvent.ReadingBelowFatalThreshold",
                "Args": [
                    {
                        "Name": "SENSOR_NAME",
                        "Type": "sdbusplus::message::object_path"
                    },
                    {
                        "Name": "READING_VALUE",
                        "Type": "double"
                    },
                    {
                        "Name": "UNITS",
                        "Type": "sdbusplus::common::xyz::openbmc_project::sensor::Value::Unit"
                    },
                    {
                        "Name": "THRESHOLD_VALUE",
                        "Type": "double"
                    }
                ]
            },
}
```

As you can see, it contains Dbus message ID/name, Redfish event registry+entry name, the DBus message should be mapped to and args vector. The args vector contains elements with Name and Type. The name of the element is a key in DBus message's AdditionalData map (that unordered_map type represents it), the type is a type of the element.
In the example above,  "xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.ReadingBelowUpperSoftShutdownThreshold" DBus message should be translated to SensorEvent.X.X.ReadingBelowFatalThreshold redfish message id. That message ID is supposed to have 4 arguments. The mapping says, that the first redfish argument should be taken from dbusMessage.additionalData["SENSOR_NAME"], the second argument from dbusMessage.additionalData["READING_VALUE"] and so on.

Changes we made in scripts/parse_registries.py consume this data from the jsons and generate corresponding structures in BMCWeb, so the code would be able to map dbus name -> redfish message ID, and know, which AdditionalData map keys the arguments should be read from.

Here is an example of a DBus message BMCWeb receives - https://gist.github.com/ifel/b0fe972e7d59ee9ded20aac58aa60bf2
It will be translated to https://gist.github.com/ifel/cbcf1f63d750f3e187f19c728a376153

> std::string_view argType; <- needs retained in both cases.

This makes total sense to me, the trouble though is, they are not the same semantically. In the example above, DBus types are double and dbus enum name/object while corresponding Redfish types for those events are number and string. So, we cannot combine them and still have to store these. These types actually do not make much of sense anyways, as the AdditionalData type is unordered_map<string, string>, MessageArgs type in Redfish is an array<string>. So we receive only strings from DBus and return to the user, so the type here sort of suggests what should be inside. The purpose of keeping DBus types is, we can (current implementation does not do that) strip type prefix (like "xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value.Unit.DegreesC" can be stripped to "DegreesC"), and potentially can be converted say from DegreesC to DegreesF, but this is something Patrick has in his mind for further improvements.

> Can you elaborate on what the dbusMessageName arg would be or do? I expected that PDI -> messageId translation would be a mechanical transform (snake case to CamelCase, etc).

I see your point. But it's not the case. I checked the map, and see no clear pattern there:
```
xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Cleared -> OpenBMC_Logging.Cleared
xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.InvalidSensorReading -> SensorEvent.InvalidSensorReading
xyz.openbmc_project.State.Leak.Detector.LeakDetectedNormal -> Environmental.LeakDetectedNormal
```

If we did mechanical mapping, your suggestion to use existing structure would've made total sense - we got DBus event and know its name, we could've mechanically get a Registry name and Entry name in the registry from the DBus event name, fetched the entry, and get dbus additional data structure keys for the arguments stored in the existing structure. However, as it cannot be done mechanically, we need that additional map to find out a registry name and an entry name in the registry.
What to the binary size, I get the concern, that's why, I originally stored the DBus event names with stripped prefix "xyz.openbmc_project.". We still duplicate some strings (like Registry and Registry Entry names) in the maps, but it's a price for a quick look up and not traversing all the registries we had to do if we could store DBus event names in the existing structures. Moreover, correct me if I'm wrong, I'm not an expert in Elf, but I was under impression that compiler stores static strings once, and just puts pointers to it, if that's true, then there are no duplicates, and it's only a matter of maintaining an additional structure which is being generated.
minor comments.
How does this stay up to date if we're pulling this from github directly?
Nvm, bad comment.

Some issues with this structure:
1. It's going to consume memory the whole time bmcweb is running
2. It needs to be constructed/malloced/sorted at startup which effects the startup time on socket activation.

Please look at the existing Registry structures and model your code after them.  They don't have either of these problems, give essentially the same result.

If there's modifications we need to make to them, great, but I don't want to maintain two different structure definitions for storing a "registry" in the binary.

I will look into making this static.

But I think we need a separate structure to make it efficient (see my point about this in the previous comment).

see my last comment above.  Happy to have efficiency discussions and "better data structure" discussions.  Lets have them in a commit message with some testing so we can show:
A. How much extra code we have to maintain to get this performance.
B. How much performance we get out of it.

And we can make a maintainability tradeoff.

I replied above. Option to reuse existing structure will require adding more code as well. I see only getRegistryFromPrefix and getMessageFromRegistry, but to implement traversal over registries, we will need to implement getAllRegistries, and traversal code.
I'm just going to close this out to avoid duplication.  Resolving the above discussion will resolve this one.

This script currently doesn't use type hints.  If you'd like to refactor it to use them consistently, I'm in support of that, but I'd like to see it done in another commit.  Up to you if it happens before or after this feature add.
